boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Michigan-Ann Arbor, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A walkable, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence connecting Central Campus and downtown Ann Arbor through public places and recurring activities.

cards.title: Start at the Michigan Union
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · Central Campus
cards.notes: Use the Union as a first indoor waypoint: orient yourself, browse the historic halls, and find the Campus Information Center before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A central gathering place with student services, eateries, and study space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Michigan Union at 530 S. State Street has study and meeting spaces, eateries, shops, student services, and the IdeaHub.
cards.access_notes: University Unions lists building hours daily; check the page for holiday or break adjustments.

cards.title: Walk the Diag
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Central Campus
cards.notes: Cross the Diag slowly and use its landmarks to build your campus bearings; the Block M, libraries, and Angell Hall are all on this route.
cards.short_summary: The heart of Central Campus and a practical landmark walk.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M’s tour identifies the Diag as Central Campus’s heart, with the Block M and nearby Hatcher, Shapiro, Angell, and other buildings.
cards.access_notes: An outdoor campus route; follow posted campus guidance and use accessible paths as needed.

cards.title: Pause at the Law Quad
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · South State Street
cards.notes: Take in the courtyard and Tudor Gothic exterior, then continue toward State Street; treat study areas as active academic spaces and keep the visit quiet.
cards.short_summary: A historic academic quadrangle near UMMA and Central Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M describes the Law Quad at 625 S. State Street as Tudor Gothic and notes that students use its spaces to relax and study.
cards.access_notes: The quad contains active law-school spaces; respect posted access and quiet-study expectations.

cards.entity_name: University of Michigan Museum of Art
cards.title: See art at UMMA
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · 525 S. State Street
cards.notes: Choose a gallery or two instead of rushing the building. Check in on arrival, use the museum map, and keep flash off if you take photos.
cards.short_summary: A free art museum visit steps from the Union and Law Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: UMMA states that admission is always free, tickets are not required, and non-flash photography is allowed in the galleries.
cards.source_title: Visit — University of Michigan Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Free admission; gallery hours vary by day and the museum is closed Mondays, so verify the visit page before going.

cards.title: Find the Michigan League fountain
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · North Central Campus
cards.notes: Walk past the stained glass and courtyard, then find the Sunday Morning in Deep Waters fountain outside for a clear campus photo landmark.
cards.short_summary: A historic student union with distinctive architecture and an outdoor fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: University Unions identifies the Michigan League as a student union known for historic architecture, stained glass, courtyard garden, and its front fountain.
cards.access_notes: Building hours differ by day; check the official page before planning an indoor stop.

cards.title: Browse the Saturday market
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · 315 Detroit Street
cards.notes: Make this an early Saturday stop. Browse the farm, food, and artisan stalls, and bring a payment method only if you plan to buy something.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Saturday market near Kerrytown with seasonal vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Saturday market hours year-round at 315 Detroit Street, with Wednesday markets also running May through December.
cards.source_title: Ann Arbor Farmers Market — City of Ann Arbor
cards.access_notes: Saturday hours are 8 a.m.–3 p.m. January–April and 7 a.m.–3 p.m. May–December; purchases are optional.

cards.title: Take a downtown library break
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Fifth and William
cards.notes: Use the Downtown Library for a reset: browse the shelves, look for current exhibits, or settle into one of the public seating areas before dinner.
cards.short_summary: A public downtown stop with collections, seating, exhibits, and study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: AADL lists the Downtown Library at 343 South Fifth Avenue and says all locations are open for browsing, seating, checkout, and phone calls daily.
cards.source_title: Locations & Hours — Ann Arbor District Library
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are 10 a.m.–8 p.m. daily, except closures; verify the current closures page before visiting.

cards.entity_name: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History
cards.title: Meet the dinosaurs at UMMNH
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Biological Sciences Building
cards.notes: Plan a self-guided loop through the exhibits, then check the museum map for temporary closures before deciding whether to add a planetarium program.
cards.short_summary: A free natural-history museum with exhibits ranging from molecules to dinosaurs.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum says individual and family admission is free and describes exhibits spanning molecules, dinosaurs, a planetarium, and science demonstrations.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information — U-M Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: Free for individuals and families; September–May hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., with Monday closure.

cards.title: Walk the Arb trails
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 1610 Washington Heights
cards.notes: Choose one trail or garden area and carry water. Start with a trail map at an entrance, stay on marked paths, and leave time to return before sunset.
cards.short_summary: A 123-acre campus landscape of trails, gardens, river access, and seasonal blooms.
cards.evidence_claim: U-M’s Nichols Arboretum page describes a 123-acre landscape with trails, gardens, natural areas, riverfront access, and free daily admission.
cards.source_title: Nichols Arboretum — Matthaei Botanical Gardens & Nichols Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Free and open daily from sunrise to sunset; use the official trail map and observe posted conditions.

cards.title: Finish along the Huron River
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 301 E. Huron Street
cards.notes: Take the riverside paths or the Argo Pond walk for a final outdoor loop. Stay on open trails, observe park rules, and avoid river activity in unsafe conditions.
cards.short_summary: A 22-acre Huron River park with trails, paths, and the Argo Cascades.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Argo as a 22-acre riverfront park and nature area with trails, paths, the Argo Pond walk, and the nine-drop Argo Cascades.
cards.source_title: Argo Park & Nature Area — City of Ann Arbor
cards.access_notes: Park hours are 6 a.m.–10 p.m. The City prohibits alcohol and requires dogs to be leashed; heed posted closures and river advisories.
